description: Between **1919** and **1933**, the **Bauhaus** school merges art, craftsmanship and industry in Germany. Closed by the Nazis, it nevertheless spread modern design throughout the world.

hero.hook: A 14-year-old German school has designed the modern world, from chairs to smartphones.

blocks.text: The **Bauhaus** (1919-1933) is the most influential art and design school of the 20th century. Founded in Germany just after the First World War, it rejects the unnecessary 19th century decor. His goal: to invent a simple language, adapted to the industrial age.
By merging art, craftsmanship and technique, it lays the foundations of the modern . His life is brief. His legacy is everywhere. [[Functionalism in design]]

In **1919**, the architect **Walter Gropius** founded the Bauhaus in **Weimar**. His manifesto is clear: the final goal of all creation is architecture. No more boundaries between noble “fine arts” and secondary “applied arts”. Craft becomes the basis of everything.

blocks.caption: The Bauhaus: a school where you learn by making.

blocks.text: Each workshop has two masters: an artist and a craftsman. Figures like , a Russian abstract painter, teach there. The school also dialogues with , a Dutch movement obsessed with the rectangle and pure colors. [[Wassily Kandinsky]] [[De Stijl]]

sections.title: Weimar 1919: abolishing the hierarchy of the arts

blocks.text: Then installed at **Dessau**, the school turned to mass production. Famous slogan: **“form follows function”**. The ornament is considered unnecessary. We are looking for simple, beautiful objects that can be manufactured in a factory.
**Marcel Breuer**, teacher at the Bauhaus, recycles tubular steel from bicycles to invent lightweight chairs. Factory material becomes living room furniture.
The workshops test metal, glass, textiles and typography. The goal is no longer the single luxury object. It is the typical object, accessible to the greatest number of people.

School is annoying. He is accused of being too modern, too international, too left-wing. After a stint in Berlin under **Mies van der Rohe**, comes . The regime sees this as “cultural Bolshevism”. [[Closure by the Nazis (1933)]]

blocks.caption: Mies van der Rohe: last leadership of the Bauhaus, then American exile.

blocks.text: Closure becomes diffusion. The masters go to the United States, Great Britain, Palestine. In Tel Aviv, their ideas nourish the , a vast ensemble of white modern architecture. [[White City of Tel Aviv]]

sections.title: Closed by the Nazis, saved by exile

blocks.text: Today, the Bauhaus heritage is everywhere: flat-pack furniture, simple buildings, clear interfaces, [[sans-serif]]  typographies. IKEA, airports, our telephones: the geometric clarity of the Bauhaus has become the ordinary decor of the world.

events.detail: Exile spreads Bauhaus throughout the world.
events.title: Nazi closure

blocks.text: In just 14 years, the Bauhaus invented the modern idea of ​​design: less ornament, more function, objects that are beautiful because they are useful. Its political closure has only accelerated its conquest of everyday life.

sections.title: A design that has become invisible through obviousness
